parts.name: Steel frame
parts.description: Cheap and strong, but heavy.

parts.name: Titanium frame
parts.description: Light, but expensive, and carries less than steel.

parts.name: Solid aluminium wheels
parts.description: Cheap and heavy. Lower grip in soft regolith.

parts.name: Wire-mesh wheels
parts.description: Light, fast and grippy, like the Apollo rover's. Bulky.

parts.name: Grouser wheels
parts.description: Deep cleats that grip loose sand. Slower than wire mesh, heavy and bulky.

parts.name: Fixed solar panel
parts.description: A flat panel. Catches little of a low Sun.

parts.name: Vertical solar mast
parts.description: Faces the low polar Sun. Light, expensive and bulky.

parts.name: Deployable solar arrays
parts.description: Folding wings of solar cells: the most solar income in sunlight. Nothing at night, less in a dust storm. Bulky.

parts.name: Radioisotope generator (RTG)
parts.description: Steady power from decaying plutonium, day and night. Its waste heat also keeps the rover warm. Expensive and heavy.

parts.name: Nickel-hydrogen battery
parts.description: Proven and cheap. Stores the most, but heavy.

parts.name: Lithium-ion battery
parts.description: Light, but expensive and stores less.

parts.name: Larger battery pack
parts.description: Stores the most, enough to keep going through a night. Light for its size, but expensive.

parts.name: LED floodlights
parts.description: Lets the rover see inside shadowed craters.

parts.name: Radioisotope heater units
parts.description: Steady heat from decaying isotopes. Slows freezing in the cold.

parts.name: Electric heater
parts.description: Cheap and light, but it runs on the battery every night, even while the rover sleeps.

parts.name: No arm
parts.description: Saves cost, mass, and space. Instruments that touch rocks cannot be carried.

parts.name: Robotic arm
parts.description: Holds contact instruments against a rock, like the arms of NASA's Curiosity and Perseverance. Takes no mounting point.

parts.name: No mast
parts.description: Saves cost, mass, and space. Instruments that work from a distance cannot be carried.

parts.name: Remote sensing mast
parts.description: A tall mast for instruments that work from a distance. Takes no mounting point.

parts.name: Science camera
parts.description: Photos and imaging science.

parts.name: Regolith drill
parts.description: Samples the soil, and ice where it exists. Heavier and bulkier than the camera.

parts.name: Neutron spectrometer
parts.description: Senses hydrogen in the top meter of soil while the rover drives, as NASA's VIPER rover is designed to do. A live meter that draws energy while switched on.

parts.name: X-ray spectrometer
parts.description: Reads a rock's main elements: park beside a boulder and hold still.

parts.name: Seismometer station
parts.description: Set it down on the ground before the moonquake to record it. Its mass leaves the rover.

parts.name: Laser retroreflector
parts.description: Mirrors for lasers fired from Earth. Needs no power; set it down where Earth is in view. Its mass leaves the rover.

parts.name: Weather mast
parts.description: Records pressure, wind and dust in the air. A switch that draws a little energy while on.

parts.name: Ground-penetrating radar
parts.description: Images the buried layers under the path while the rover drives. Draws energy while switched on.

parts.name: Laser spectrometer
parts.description: Zaps a rock from a few meters away and reads its elements in the flash.

parts.name: Organics spectrometer
parts.description: Looks for organic molecules in a rock. A long, slow reading that costs a lot of energy.
